feedback: Pre-race review of the iteration 7 candidate. It keeps the iteration 6 design (best raced at 354.2: narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03; sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2]; base_speed 1.1; kp 2.0; ki 0; last_direction) and changes one variable, kd from 0.3 to 0.25. Iteration 6 showed that kp 2.5 to 2.0 cut oval line_loss_events (0.95 to 0.85), oval max_error (0.054 to 0.048) and s-bend line loss (1.25 to 1.1), while oval completion rose to 16 of 20. Its oval steering_oscillation of 0.327 is the highest jitter reading, and iteration 4 (kd 0.3, kp 2.5) gave the same 0.327, so kd is the next untested lever. Iteration 3 (kd 0.25 with kp 2.2 at base_speed 1.3) lost line and scored 106.7, but it also changed kp and speed, so it does not isolate kd. Iteration 5 showed that base_speed 0.9 hurts completion, so speed stays at 1.1. Iteration 2 showed that the wide array does not help, so the geometry is kept. The candidate is valid, within contract limits, and a clean one-variable step from the best design, so it is approved. Nothing about its performance can be read from the earlier races; the race is the test. Next step, depending on the race: if oval steering_oscillation falls and line_loss_events and max_error stay at or below iteration 6 levels, keep kd 0.25 and test a larger line-loss fix for the s-bend and slalom, such as a separate small kp change. If line_loss_events or max_error rise, revert kd to 0.3 and test base_speed 1.2 alone, since 1.1 and 1.3 are the only tested speeds near that range.
requested_changes: If the race shows line_loss_events and max_error at or below iteration 6 levels (0.85 and 0.048 on the oval) with lower oscillation, keep kd 0.25 and vary kp only in a small step (about 1.8) to see whether the s-bend (line loss 1.1) and slalom (line loss 1.0) improve, since iteration 6 showed kp reduction helped line retention.

If line_loss_events or max_error rise with kd 0.25, revert kd to 0.3 and test base_speed 1.2 alone, since iteration 6 at kd 0.3 is the best raced baseline and iteration 1 at 1.3 and iteration 4 at 1.1 are the only controlled speed comparisons.
Keep the narrow five-sensor geometry and sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] unchanged in either case, since iteration 2 (wide array, 22.5 mm spacing) dropped the score to 81.1 without improving line loss.
